candidate_evidence.quote: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of neoadjuvant radiochemotherapy in the surgical resection of glioblastoma (GBM).
4 weeks post-surgery, temozolomide (TMZ) will be administered for 6 months

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Stereotactic biopsy will be performed, and if GBM is diagnosed, patients will undergo conformal hypofractionated stereotactic radiotherapy

role_evidence.quote: with a total dose of 3990 cGy at the margin in 15 fractions of 266 cGy, one session per day, five days a week, and concurrent temozolomide (TMZ) at 75 mg/m2/day for 7 days/week during the irradiation period (GEINO, 2016)
4 weeks post-surgery, temozolomide (TMZ) will be administered for 6 months

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent (established GBM therapy) given neoadjuvantly with hypofractionated RT before resection

role_evidence.quote: temozolomide (TMZ) will be administered for 6 months according to the Stupp protocol.

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent (established GBM therapy), standard Stupp control

role_evidence.quote: supramarginal resection guided by 5-ALA under intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring

source_quote.quote: If the histopathological diagnosis is not wildtype IDH non-mutated glioblastoma, the patient will be withdrawn from the study and receive conventional treatment.

coder_notes: The investigational question is the sequencing (neoadjuvant hypofractionated RT + concurrent TMZ before resection) versus standard Stupp; temozolomide is the only drug and its schedule differs between arms, so rule 6 (established_therapy_experiment). 5-ALA is not a separately registered drug intervention; it is listed because the 'resection' intervention (in both arms) is described as 5-ALA guided. IDH-wildtype is a GBM-defining criterion applied after biopsy in the experimental arm.
